en: In the City of Destruction, a man sat reading a Book. The more he read, the heavier his heart grew.
This Book says our city will be burned with fire from heaven. What shall I do to be saved?
And this burden on my back grows heavier every day.
You are tired, that is all. Sleep, and you will feel better in the morning.
Stay with them, or go?
Stay and hope the city improves
Leave and find the way
He dreamed of red smoke over the rooftops. When he woke, the burden was heavier still.
Flee from the wrath to come.
There goes the man with the Book again.
He has gone soft in the head, poor fellow.
Neighbour, where are you going? Come back with us!
I am going to an inheritance that cannot fade away. Come with me.
Tush! Away with your Book. Will you come back with us or no?
No, not I. I have laid my hand to the plough.
Come, Pliable, let us go home. I will not keep company with such a fool.
Wait. If what he says is true, things are better where he is going. I will go with him.
Then you are both fools. I am going home.
Tell me more of the place we are going. Is it truly so good?
There is a kingdom there that will never end, and crowns of glory for those who reach it.
Why are you crying?
Sir, I read that I am condemned to die and after that to come to judgement. I am not ready.
Then why do you stand still?
Because I do not know which way to go.
Do you see yonder wicket gate?
No.
Do you see yonder shining light?
I think I do.
Keep that light in your eye, and go straight toward it. There you will find the gate. Knock, and you will be told what to do.
Read the Book when you are unsure of the way. It will show you what you cannot see.
So he began to run, crying, 'Life, life, eternal life!'
